findings.claim: Open Targets gives a moderate IL23A–Crohn disease association score (0.61), driven almost entirely by clinical-stage evidence (0.99); literature 0.245 and RNA expression 0.043 are low.
findings.supportingPassage: Overall association score 0.61 (datatypes: clinical 0.99, literature 0.245, rna_expression 0.043)
findings.limitations: Scores rank evidence and are not probabilities of success; the clinical score reflects drug trials, not independent genetic evidence.

findings.claim: Risankizumab is an IL-23 inhibitor antibody acting on IL-23 (including p19/IL23A, Q9NPF7); ChEMBL max phase 4 overall (first approval 2019) with Crohn's disease listed at max phase 3 in this record.
findings.supportingPassage: Mechanism: Interleukin-23 inhibitor (INHIBITOR; target Interleukin-23 P29460,Q9NPF7)
findings.limitations: Max phase is development stage, not efficacy; the ChEMBL Crohn's indication phase may lag regulatory status.

findings.claim: Phase 3 ADVANCE and MOTIVATE induction trials (IV risankizumab 600/1200 mg vs placebo, weeks 0/4/8) met all co-primary endpoints at week 12 (clinical remission and endoscopic response) in moderate-to-severe Crohn's disease; in MOTIVATE (biologic-failure population) CDAI remission was 42%/40% vs 20% placebo and endoscopic response 29%/34% vs 11%.
findings.supportingPassage: All coprimary endpoints at week 12 were met in both trials with both doses of risankizumab (p values ≤0·0001).
findings.population: Adults 16-80 y; ADVANCE: biologic or conventional failure; MOTIVATE: biologic failure
findings.endpoint: Week 12 clinical remission and endoscopic response
findings.studyContext: Randomised double-masked placebo-controlled phase 3; sponsor AbbVie
findings.limitations: Sponsor-funded; 12-week induction; placebo-controlled, no active comparator; registry results table has duplicated/mislabelled US vs global rows so the paper was used for numbers.

findings.claim: In the FORTIFY randomised withdrawal maintenance trial (SC risankizumab q8w, induction responders), 360 mg beat placebo withdrawal at week 52 for CDAI remission (52% vs 41%) and endoscopic response (47% vs 22%).
findings.supportingPassage: Greater clinical remission and endoscopic response rates were reached with 360 mg risankizumab versus placebo
findings.endpoint: Week 52 clinical remission and endoscopic response
findings.limitations: Withdrawal design compares to patients withdrawn from drug (placebo remission 41% is high due to prior response); enriched responder population; sponsor-funded.

findings.claim: Not all benefit is large or uniform: in FORTIFY, the 180 mg dose did not significantly beat withdrawal on stool-frequency/abdominal-pain remission (p=0.124), and the absolute remission gain vs placebo in induction (~15–22 points) leaves most patients not in remission; the most common AEs included worsening Crohn's disease.
findings.supportingPassage: but not stool frequency and abdominal pain score clinical remission [p=0·124]
findings.limitations: One secondary-type comparison for one dose; other co-primary endpoints were met.

findings.claim: No experimental structure of risankizumab bound to IL23A was found; an AlphaFold model of IL23A (mean pLDDT 80.56) was selected, which is structural confidence only and not disease relevance.

gaps.description: Could not retrieve a head-to-head trial (e.g., risankizumab vs ustekinumab) or long-term safety/real-world data in a form that supports comparative claims; real-world studies appeared in search but were not read.
